results.evidence: The button calls `moveToDraft`, which runs `hogFlowsPartialUpdate(..., { status: 'draft' })`. `isReadOnly` is `broadcast.status !== 'draft'`, so the wizard becomes editable. The summary says "Draft schedules are left in place", and no backend change was made. Whether the scheduler skips draft flows is not shown, so I can't confirm the send stops.

The button condition is `broadcast?.status === 'active' && !batchJobsLoading && !hasInFlightJob`. It never checks for a pending schedule. It would also show for an immediate send, or a completed one-time schedule, that is still active.

After activation: `for (const existing of activated.schedules ?? []) { await hogFlowsSchedulesDestroy(...) }`. Then `hogFlowsSchedulesCreate` makes one new schedule for 'later' or 'recurring'. For 'now' only the batch job is created, so no schedule is left behind.

`hogFlowsPartialUpdate(projectId, broadcastId, { status: 'active' })` runs before the schedule destroy and create calls. An interruption between them, such as a page close, leaves the broadcast active. The catch block reverts to draft only when the code can still run.
Only in-flight jobs (`hasInFlightJob`) and `batchJobsLoading` are guarded. Nothing checks for more than one schedule or for a workflow shape the wizard can't safely edit.
`onClick={moveToDraft}` dispatches the action directly. There is no confirmation dialog.
`moveToDraft` only patches the status and shows the single toast 'Broadcast moved to draft'. It never cancels a started batch job, and there are no warning or failure variants.
The patch changes only two frontend files. There is no scheduler change and no status re-check before a run is created.
The new schedule is built only from `rrule`, `starts_at` and `timezone`. Existing schedules are destroyed without reading their variables, so any overrides are dropped.

result:
Users can now move a live, scheduled broadcast back to draft, and launching now replaces any existing schedule with a fresh active one. I didn't run tests or type-checking, and I added no tests. Only frontend files changed, so the backend has no new endpoint and no way to resume a paused schedule.

**Launch fix** (`products/workflows/frontend/Broadcasts/broadcastWizardLogic.ts`)
- After the broadcast is activated, `launchBroadcast` deletes every existing schedule on it, using the schedules the activation response returns. It then creates the one chosen in the wizard, or none for "send now".
- A schedule paused by an audience edit is therefore deleted and rebuilt as active, so a relaunched broadcast no longer looks live while never sending.

**Back to draft** (`broadcastWizardLogic.ts`, `BroadcastSummary.tsx`)
- I added a `moveToDraft` action with a `movingToDraft` loading state. It sets the broadcast's status to `draft`, stores the result, and moves to the first invalid step, or to review if none. The scene then shows the wizard, so the details can be edited.
- The read-only summary now has a "Move to draft" button beside the status tag. It appears only while the broadcast is active and no send is queued or running.
- Draft schedules are left in place, and a relaunch replaces them.

I hand-edited the kea-typegen interface blocks in the logic file to match the new action and value, as the file's own comments allow.
